key_insight: Three-dimensional DSMC captures measured jet–crossflow interference pressure, while two-dimensional modeling reproduces qualitative patterns but overpredicts peak pressure about twelvefold.
engineering_relevance: Accurate prediction of reaction-control-jet interference in rarefied hypersonic flight requires three-dimensional kinetic modeling rather than planar approximations.
method: Revisited a 1975 DLR helium-jet experiment in Mach 11–12 air crossflow.
Compared two- and three-dimensional DSMC across three freestream densities at Knudsen numbers of 0.021–0.125.
Checked planar resolution convergence and plate-alone boundary-layer consistency.
evidence_signal: Across all three densities, three-dimensional DSMC reproduced the measured interference-pressure lobe peak within 25% and its position within 3 mm.
watch_item: Both models overpredict plate-alone wall pressure by 50–75%, and lateral relief remains an unconfirmed explanation for the planar model’s interference-pressure error.
paper_title: Kinetic study of Reaction-Control-Jet Interference in Rarefied Hypersonic Crossflow
